subject: Constrained multi response regression using brms?

messages.author: 7e538b23746d6b75
messages.subject: Constrained multi response regression using brms?
parts:
Dear forum,

I have a designed experiment, where I combine all possible pairs, triplets, an quartets, of seven bacterial strains. Each combination is a separet experiment. After growth and subsequent harvest, the relative composition of strains in each experiment is measure using a dna technique.

The purpose of this experiment is to predict the strain composition of new blends of up to seven strains, and the interaction structure between strains, i.e. If the presence of a strain inhibits or stimulates other strains in a given blend.

My design matrix therefore consist of seven columns and 96 rows, one row for each experiment. Each column represents a strain, and the presence or absence of this strain in the inocolum is decoded as 1 and 0, respectively.

The response matrix also consists of seven columns and 96 rows. Each column in the response matrix represents the relative composition of each strain in the final blend after growth in co-culture.

The response, for each strain is therefore constrianed between zero and one, and the sum of the relative compositions of strains is by definition always one. That is, the responses are strongly correlated.

I can figure out how to fit the response of a single strain in brms using Beta regression, but I cannot figure if its possible to impose the sum to one contstraint between the responses.

Is it possible to constrain the responses between one and zero and at the same time forcing the responses to sum to one using brms?

Any ideas would be highly appreciated.

Regards

/jannik

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Constrained multi response regression using brms?
parts:
This is not yet possible in brms, but it would come to something one may call "dirichlet regression" since the dirichlet distribution is exactly what you are describing (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirichlet_distribution).

I will think about adding this to brms in version 2.0.0+ after I added full support for multivariate models (not just for gaussian ones).
